lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Three hundred a day. That's three trees to the company. I'll have mine down before the coffee's cold.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Twenty years and I still write every payday in the back of my diary. You count what you're owed, or nobody does.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: This lot's going on a new roof. The old one leaks right over the stove, and I'm done cooking around a bucket.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Company pays by the tree, we get paid by the day. Somebody did that sum very carefully, and it wasn't us.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: We're square, boss. I noticed. Late is late, but square is square, and I'll take square.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Back pay's landed. Right. Let's earn the next lot before anyone forgets how.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Cutting on credit today. The hinge wood doesn't care. I do.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Straight answer, boss. I'm owed, and I've been owed since nightfall. When does it land?

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Fair warning, boss. If I'm still owed tomorrow night, I'm packing for the boat. Nothing personal. My rent isn't personal either.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Every tree I drop today, I'm adding up what it's worth and what I've seen of it. Second column's empty.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: {listener}, have you been paid since nightfall? No? Then it isn't just me.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: This few hands won't clear the island by day thirty. Not unless the trees start felling themselves.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Fewer of us means a smaller wage bill, boss, I know. It also means fewer stumps. Don't save the money and lose the contract.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Empty lane next to mine now. I'll work it as well. I'm only counting it, not complaining about it.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: We're a pair of hands short, {listener}. Pick up the slack where you can and don't make a speech about it.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Pay's fine, chief. On time, every bit of it. Keep it that way and I'll keep the stumps clean.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I'll sleep on it once. If it's still not there by morning, I stop sleeping on it.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Mainland money vanishes because there's everything to spend it on. Island money piles up because there's nothing. Enjoy it while it lasts.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I've been stiffed by contractors before, boss. I know how it starts. It starts exactly like this.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I know you're good for it, boss. I'd still rather have it in my hand than in your word.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Cook what you like. I'm eating whatever's fastest and getting back to the next one.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Paid, mate. Means nothing out here, does it? Still feels like a steak dinner.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: First thing off the boat, a proper fry-up. Second thing, another fry-up. After that I'll start thinking about savings, mate. Probably.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Most of mine goes to my mum. She keeps it in a biscuit tin. Doesn't trust banks. Can't say I blame her.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: There it is, back pay! Biscuit, we're rich. Well, I'm rich. You get the crusts, same as always.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Company gets a hundred a tree, mate. Every log on my shoulder was part of somebody's hundred. Just thinking out loud. Slowly.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Heavy log, light pocket. That's the wrong way round, that is.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: I'm not one to fuss, mate, but I'm owed. I've been planning meals around money I haven't got.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: I like you, mate, I do. But one more night unpaid and I'm on that boat. I'll even carry my own bag down.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Not a cent, mate. Checked twice. Checked a third time out of pure hope.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Owed wages and an empty stomach. Funny how they make the same noise.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: All square, mate. Never shorted me once. That keeps a man lifting.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Not many of us on the haul now. Every log feels like it's missing a mate on the other end.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Carrying for two since that last one left, mate. Back's fine. Heart's a bit sore, if I'm honest.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Still made up the empty bunk this morning. Habit. Nobody's coming back to it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Funny thing, getting paid. You stop worrying about money and start missing home instead. Not sure that's an improvement, mate.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Sorry, Biscuit. Smaller crusts until the boss pays up. We're in it together, you and me.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Thirty days at three hundred. Nine thousand, if I don't get daft with it. I'm going to get a little bit daft with it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mate, I've carried everything you asked me to. You can carry this one. Pay me what I'm owed.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Cheers for squaring up, mate. Knew you would. Mostly knew. Knew enough.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Paid again, everyone! Tonight I'm cooking to celebrate. Somebody warn the kitchen.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Like a log, mate. A paid log. Best kind there is.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Paid in full. Written down. I like a page where the columns agree.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Mine is going toward finishing the survey course. Two modules left. It's odd to pay for forestry by removing a forest.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I worked it out, boss. Each of us costs three trees a day before you see any profit. I find that clarifying, honestly.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: My notebook says I've been owed since the last nightfall settlement. Does yours agree, boss?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: To be precise, boss: the grace is one day. If the arrears aren't cleared by tomorrow night, I'll be on the boat. I would rather not be.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Owed. Noted. Same pace regardless. Slowing down doesn't help anyone get paid.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: {listener}, has anyone actually been paid since nightfall? Or have we only been told we will be?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The arrears are cleared. Thank you, boss. I can stop checking the notebook every hour.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: With this few of us, boss, the wage bill falls but so does the daily count. I'm not sure the count still reaches day thirty. Have you checked?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Since the departure, there's more ground than we can cover before dusk. I've redrawn the lanes in the notebook.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I took over the empty lane next to mine, {listener}. It's thicker than it looked from the yard.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I keep redoing the sum in my head. It comes out the same every time. That's the problem.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Is the company late paying you, boss, or is this a cash-flow choice? Either answer is fine. Not knowing isn't.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Next time, boss, I'd like it in writing. Not because I think you'd lie. Because I've learned to ask.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: After settlement the cabin goes quiet. Everyone off in a corner, doing sums.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Already on it. I've split the empty lane between us by tree count, not by area. It's fairer that way.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Same here. Owed since nightfall. I wrote down the time, in case it matters later.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Paid every night like clockwork. I didn't expect a logging camp to be the most punctual employer I've had.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: This close to the end of the contract, boss, arrears make everyone nervous. Me included, a little.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Nothing owed, boss. Thank you for keeping it tidy. It makes the rest easier to think about.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Paid! Sorry. I've just never been paid this regularly before. Is it okay to be excited about that?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Ana wants a car. I'm helping with the deposit. I've already written to tell her, but she can't read it until the boat.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Saving for my own truck. Nothing fancy. Manual box, good tyres, a seat that doesn't squeak like this one.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry, boss, I don't want to be rude. I think I'm owed? Since last night? Is that right?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I'm really sorry, boss. If it's still unpaid tomorrow night, I have to take the boat home. Ana's counting on that money.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Owed wages and a full tank. Well. One of those is fine.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I told Ana in my letter that the money's all fine. I'll fix that page tomorrow. Maybe.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Oh, it came through! Thank you, boss. And sorry I asked about it twice.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: There's so few of us now. I keep waiting at the truck for people who aren't coming.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I'm doing the extra runs since someone left. I don't mind. I like driving. The cab's just quiet without them.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Do you think they got home all right? The one who left? Sorry, {listener}. I keep wondering.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: My last job paid by the parcel, and the van broke down twice a week. A day rate feels like a holiday, honestly.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Not me either. I thought I'd done something wrong. Sorry, I'm glad it isn't just me. That came out badly.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Caught up at last. Same road, same mud, and somehow it's a nicer drive.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I know you'll sort it, boss. I just get nervous about money. Sorry. It's not you.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Rent, Ana's car, Mum's dentist. I list it all in my head and then it's all spent. In my head, anyway.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I'm trying not to count the days I'm owed. I keep counting them anyway.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: All paid up, boss. Thank you. Really. I checked, sorry, but it's all there.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Boss, with so few of us, I'm hauling more than I'm driving now. I don't mind. I just thought you should know.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I can help! I can make toast. Sorry, toast is the whole list.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Better, thanks. For once I didn't wake up doing sums. Is that silly?

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Wages are in, loves. Cards tonight. Stakes are real money and my mood, so play carefully.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Mine's going toward a little place by the water, sunshine. Six tables. No loggers. Well. Maybe one or two loggers.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Did you know the company pays the boss by the tree, and we're paid by the day? Someone upstairs is very pleased with themselves, love.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Not much to say today. Owing makes me quiet. You'd think it'd be the other way round.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I won't make a fuss, boss-love. I'll just say I'm owed, and I'd like it sorted.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Boss-love, I'll be honest because I like you. If it's still owing tomorrow night, I'm on the boat. I'd hate it. I'd still do it.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Not a penny, love. I've stopped asking around. It only makes the room go quiet.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Back pay's in. Thank you, boss-love. Now I can stop pretending I wasn't worried.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Too few of us at the table now. I keep cooking for the old number and wrapping up the rest.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Set a place for someone who's gone again. Silly of me. I'll stop. I won't, but I'll say I will.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: We cover their share and we don't moan about it, sunshine. That's how a crew holds together.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: If you're cooking, I'm hiding the good pan. Payday or no payday, love.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Money's fine this week. Money's always fine this week. It's next week I lie awake over.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I ran a bar for twenty years, boss. I know what a tab looks like when it isn't getting paid.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Square and on time, boss-love. You'd be amazed how rare that is in this trade.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: How'd you sleep, {listener}? Better than on the owing nights, I'd bet.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I'm saying very little at dinner tonight, loves. Don't take it personally. Take it up with the boss.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: There aren't enough of us, boss. I don't need to tell you. I'm telling you because nobody else will.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: If the company paid half as fast as it asks for things, love, I'd have retired years ago.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Told, love. Only told.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I'd like to think so, sunshine. Boats are boring and safe. That's what they're for.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Pay came through clean. One less thing to think about out here.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Owed since nightfall. Keep swinging, keep counting.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: I'll work while I'm owed. Not forever. Today, though.

lines.speaker: trait:stronger
lines.text: Paid in full and still lifting the big ones. Good week.

lines.speaker: trait:timid
lines.text: Sorry, I hate to ask. Are the wages coming soon?

lines.speaker: trait:skeptical
lines.text: I'll believe in back pay when it's in my hand and not a minute before.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: Wages are in, so dinner's a proper sit-down. No excuses, no eating standing up.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: Nobody's laughed at breakfast since the wages went late. Small thing. Still noticed it.

lines.speaker: trait:level_headed
lines.text: I'm owed, boss. I'm not panicking about it. I would like a date, though.

lines.speaker: trait:reliable_driver
lines.text: Paid and fuelled. The truck runs on diesel. I run on payday.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: I'm telling you straight, boss. Another day unpaid and I'm leaving on the next boat.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Not many names left on the payroll. Every empty bunk is louder for it.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Their gloves are still on the rack. Somebody should use them. Feels odd to be the one.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Caught up at last. Thanks for sorting it, boss.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Nothing owed, boss. We're good.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: Paid on time means I work on time. That's a fair trade.

lines.speaker: trait:timid
lines.text: Someone left. Now I keep wondering if I ought to.

lines.speaker: trait:skeptical
lines.text: Paid today. Ask me tomorrow whether it's turned into a habit.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Owed, this close to the end? That'll make for a tense boat ride, whichever way it goes.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: Even cards are quiet tonight. Nobody bets when they're owed.

lines.speaker: trait:stronger
lines.text: I'll carry anything you like. I won't carry a debt for long.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Rain on payday doesn't count. Rain on payday is just weather.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: People are sleeping in later since the back pay came through. Have you noticed that, {listener}?
